Quick ops snapshot:
- Timeline: traffic surge at 07:48, p99 spike @ 07:50, 5xx window 07:50–07:57, recovery ~08:05.
- Root indicators: high hot-key incidence on the tenant’s KV cache (top 5 prefixes accounted for ~42% of requests in the 10m window). Continuous batching lanes for those keys were saturating hot-lane capacity; KV cache thrash observed as TTL churn + small hotset churned through cache shards.
- Symptoms: HOL blocking on hot-lane queues triggered backpressure, which cascaded into request timeouts for other lanes. No kernel-level regressions observed; the model instances reported normal CPU/GPU utilization.

Immediate mitigation enacted at 08:40:
1) Applied emergency hot-lane weight increase for Orchid tenant (+20% capacity on hot-lane pool).
2) Temporarily raised prefix KV TTL to 45s for the tenant (was 5s).
3) Enabled conservative batching (reduce max batch size by 30%) for prefixes with >200 qps.

Preliminary impact: p99 down from ~2.6s to ~340ms, 5xx stopped after mitigation window. We’re continuing to observe.

Next steps (for exec and customer): propose a short-term reserved burst and a medium-term config change: persistent hot-lane reservation + adaptive TTL rules keyed to prefix cardinality. Draft plan below for Laura to send to customer.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Hi Sara / Procurement —

Thank you for flagging this quickly and for the screenshots. Below is a succinct summary and next steps so Procurement has the facts for any credit conversation.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-10-12 07:48–07:57 PT. Root cause: hot-key driven KV cache thrash causing head-of-line (HOL) blocking in our hot-lane batch queues. This led to request queue buildup and elevated p99 and a short 5xx burst.
- Immediate mitigation: emergency hot-lane capacity increase, raised prefix TTL for Orchid tenant, reduced max batch size on problematic prefixes. Result: p99 reduced to ~340ms and 5xx rate returned to baseline.

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) 72-hour morning reservation: 06:30–09:00 PT dedicated hot-lane reservation (operational accommodation) — deploy within 2 hours on customer approval.
2) 48h data handoff: Orchid to provide a 10-minute debug log and sample payloads around 07:50 (we request within 24 hours).
3) 2–3 week engineering work: implement adaptive TTL and hotset-aware prefetcher; schedule a post-mortem and config rollout test across a staging tenant.
4) Credits: we will review SLA attachment and propose a credit calculation if the root cause is on our serving runtime; Ben will coordinate with Procurement.

Attachments: orchid_sla_request.pdf, runbook_kv_hotkey_mitigation_v2.docx (ops runbook)

Can we schedule a 30-minute call at 15:00 PT today to confirm the reservation and data handoff? Ben will send the calendar invite.
